title: Wed AM: network + GPU bubble log
content:
Morning focus (quick):
- Hot path: investigate brief spike in preemptions around 03/11 07:22 UTC (region: us-west2). suspicion: kernel driver flakiness after recent cuda-driver update.
- Confirmed: 3x pods OOMKilled on gpu-pool-b-*, all during 512-token generation runs.

Immediate todo (order):
1) Grab logs from node gpu-node-07 and gpu-node-12: sudo journalctl -u kubelet -n 1000; copy /var/log/nvidia-installer.log -> /tmp/ishaan-gpu-logs
2) Run nvidia-smi on both nodes, check retention of processes and mem usage: nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid,process_name,used_memory --format=csv
3) Put gpu-node-07 in maintenance: kubectl cordon gpu-node-07; kubectl drain gpu-node-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=5m && watch for stuck pod evictions
4) Trigger lightweight perf run on stable-2b-qa to reproduce OOM locally (512 tokens, batch size 8) — use bench-v2 script.

Quick commands crib (copy this before I forget):
- ssh core@gpu-node-07 -- 'sudo journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 | tail -n 200 > /tmp/kubelet-tail.log'
- scp core@gpu-node-07:/tmp/kubelet-tail.log ~/work/tmp/gpu-node-07-kubelet.log
- kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep gpu-node-07
- kubectl describe pod <pod> -n inference | sed -n '1,200p'

Capacity notes / numbers to check:
- Target reserved throughput for hosted SLO: 45k tokens/sec across us-west2 d/g pools this quarter. Current 72h avg: 41.8k (down 0.2k from yesterday).
- Spare headroom target = 15% -> target buffer tokens/sec = ~6.7k tokens/sec. If node drain >1 for d/g pools, alert and scale up rule should kick.
- Autoscaler policy in dedicated: min 12 GPUs, current steady = 13, max = 20. If we lose 2 nodes, headroom will be tight for bursts.

Networking quick checks:
- Observe increased retransmits on eth0 on gpu-node-12 during time window: if tcp_retransmits > 40 -> escalate to infra-net.
- Check iperf tests between us-west2-gpu-subnet and redis-caches: iperf3 -c redis-10.4.2.3 -t 20 -R

Short-term mitigation plan (if we see more OOMs):
- Rollback last driver update on affected nodes (ticket INFRA-rollback-cuda-2026-03-09). Coordinate with sre-release.
- If rollback not possible immediately, reduce default generation max_tokens to 384 for QA/stable pools for next 2 hours (via feature flag) to lower peak memory pressure.
- Increase batching timeout from 10ms -> 12ms to reduce concurrent in-flight KV cache pressure (small perf hit).

Open questions / followups:
- Did runtime change in PR #2142 touch memory allocator path for kv-cache? Marco to confirm.
- Are any customer workloads pinned to stable-2b-qa that would be affected by transient throttle? (Check account: ACCT-7201)
- Should we temporarily route critical traffic to reserved-dedicated pool until nodes stabilized? Pros/cons: cost vs latency.

Handy links + refs:
- JIRA: JIRA-INFRA-4872 (kernel driver flake)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2142 (recent allocator tweaks)
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/auto-batching-notes

Notes-to-self (random):
- If I end up rolling node back, remember to run rebench and record per-token ms in #infra-telemetry channel.
- Don't forget to ping Leah and add notes to the incident doc. Leah: check gpu pool metrics dashboard (route: /dash/pools/us-west2/gpu).
- If kernel rollback needed, schedule during low traffic window: 03/13 02:00–04:00 UTC.

End-of-shift handoff snippet:
- What I did: cordoned gpu-node-07, collected kubelet + nvidia logs, kicked a reproduce bench (ongoing).
- What I expect next: either reproduce OOM (then escalate) or see that draining resolved stuck pods and autoscaler scales up one node.
- Handoff to: Leah Kim (primary), Marco Ruiz (secondary). Slack: #infra-ops, thread 'INF-4872 kernel flake'

Misc scratch / micro-ideas:
- Could try soft-limiting per-process GPU-memory via CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES + cgroup v2 memory.max? experimental.
- Add a quick synthetic mem-pressure test to regression CI for stable-2b-qa.

---
Timestamped quick activity log (small):
2026-03-11T07:26 - noticed spikes, opened JIRA INFRA-4872
2026-03-11T07:34 - cordoned gpu-node-07 (inflight pods evicting)
2026-03-11T07:40 - pulled nvidia-installer log, saw last install 2026-03-09 03:02 UTC
2026-03-11T08:05 - started reproduce bench (512 tokens, bs=8) on qm-stable-2b-qa-01

(Okay that's enough coffee for now)
